# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 17 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Son of David — The Messianic King

---

**17:1** O LORD, you are our king forever and ever —
in you, O God, our soul finds all its glory.

**17:2** How short is the span of a man's life on earth —
all his hope is bounded by the length of his days.

**17:3** But we — we hope in God our savior;
for the power of our God endures forever in mercy,
and the kingdom of our God stands forever over the nations in judgment.

**17:4** You, O LORD, chose David as king over Israel
and swore to him concerning his seed forever:
that his dynasty would never fail before you.

**17:5** But because of our sins, sinners rose up against us,
they ambushed and drove us out —
those to whom you had given no promise;
they plundered us by force, giving no glory to your holy name.

**17:6** In their insolence they erected a kingdom,
they defiled the throne of David in riotous arrogance.

**17:7** But you, O God, toppled them — you cut their seed from the earth —
for there rose against them a man alien to our whole race.

**17:8** You paid them back, O God, according to their sins;
it fell upon them as their deeds deserved.

**17:9** God showed them no mercy;
he hunted down their seed and let not a single one escape.

**17:10** Faithful is the LORD in all his judgments
that he executes on the earth.

**17:11** The lawless one laid waste our land
so that not one soul among them practiced mercy and truth.

**17:12** They withdrew to a place of desolation;
they dared not come near our territory.

**17:13** The enemy was filled with arrogance,
and his heart was totally alienated from our God.

**17:14** Everything he was doing in Jerusalem
was exactly what the nations were doing in their own strongholds.

**17:15** And the children of the covenant, living in the midst of the mixed multitude,
none of them in Jerusalem was showing mercy or truth.

**17:16** Those who had loved the assemblies of the devout fled from them;
like sparrows startled from the nest, they flew away.

**17:17** They scattered into the wilderness to save their souls from evil;
and the life of any exile among them was precious beyond words.

**17:18** By the hand of the lawless one they were scattered across every land;
for heaven itself held back its dew and rain from the earth.

**17:19** Perennial springs went dry —
the springs that flow from the deep to the heights of the mountains —
for there was no one who practiced righteousness and justice.

**17:20** Their rulers were cut down by the sword;
not one person mourned for them,
for they were strangers to us.

**17:21** Look, O LORD — raise up for them their king,
the son of David, at the time that you know, O God —
to reign over Israel your servant!

**17:22** Gird him with strength to shatter unrighteous rulers,
to purge Jerusalem from the nations that trample her down to ruin.

**17:23** In wisdom, in righteousness, let him expel sinners from the inheritance;
let him smash the arrogance of the sinner as a potter smashes a clay jar.

**17:24** With a rod of iron let him crush their every stronghold;
with the word of his mouth let him destroy the lawless nations.

**17:25** At his rebuke, nations will scatter from before him;
he will convict sinners by exposing the very thoughts of their hearts.

**17:26** He will gather a holy people
and lead them in righteousness;
he will judge the tribes of the people that has been sanctified by the LORD his God.

**17:27** He will not permit unrighteousness to take up residence among them;
no one who knows wickedness will be allowed to live in their midst.

**17:28** For he will know them — they are all children of their God —
and he will distribute them over the land according to their tribes,

**17:29** and no foreigner or alien will dwell among them ever again.
He will judge peoples and nations in the wisdom of his righteousness. Selah.

**17:30** He will put the Gentile nations under his yoke to serve him;
he will glorify the LORD in a place visible to all the earth;

**17:31** and he will purify Jerusalem, making it holy as in the days of old,

**17:32** so that nations stream from the ends of the earth to see his glory,
bringing back as gifts her sons who had been cast to the winds,

**17:33** to see the glory of the LORD with which God has crowned her.
And he himself will be a righteous king, taught by God, ruling over them.

**17:34** In his days there will be no unrighteousness among them —
for all will be holy, and their king will be the LORD Messiah.

**17:35** For he will not put his confidence in horse or rider or bow,
nor heap up gold and silver for war,

**17:36** nor will he build his hope on multitudes of warriors for the day of battle.
The LORD himself is his king — the hope of the one whose strength rests in hope in God.

**17:37** He will show compassion to all the nations who stand trembling before him.

**17:38** For he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth forever;
he will bless the people of the LORD with wisdom and joy.

**17:39** He will himself be pure from sin so that he can rule over a great people,
rebuking rulers and cleansing sinners by the sheer power of his word.

**17:40** He will not falter in his days, for his trust is wholly in his God;
for God has made him mighty in the Holy Spirit,
wise in counsel and understanding,
with strength and righteousness.

**17:41** The blessing of the LORD is with him in power;
and his hope in the LORD will never waver.

**17:42** Who will stand against him?
He is mighty in his works and strong in the fear of God.

**17:43** He tends the flock of the LORD faithfully and righteously;
he lets none of them stumble in their pasture.

**17:44** He leads them all in equity;
there is no arrogance among them so that any would oppress another.

**17:45** This is the majesty of the king of Israel,
whom God knows, whom he raises up over the house of Israel to instruct it.

**17:46** His words will be as the words of the holy ones, in the midst of a holy people.
Blessed are those who will be born in those days,
to see the good things of Israel that God will bring to pass
in the gathering of the tribes!
May God hasten his mercy upon Israel!
May he deliver us from the pollution of profane enemies!
The LORD himself is our king forever and ever.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering of the great Messianic Psalm. Every verse rendered for full poetic impact. 'Son of David' (v.21), 'rod of iron / word of his mouth' (v.24), 'LORD Messiah' (v.34), 'Holy Spirit' (v.40) all preserved.*
